newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Top natural rubber producers meet in Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Top natural rubber producers meet in Sri Lanka.

text.p: The world's leading natural rubber producers began a meeting in Sri Lanka on Tuesday to find ways to raise consumption of natural rubber over synthetics and discuss production problems, a spokesman said.
"All the main natural rubber producers are represented at this meeting," Dr. Keerthi Tillekeratne, director of the Rubber Research Institute of Sri Lanka told Reuters.
"We will discuss ways to encourage the use of natural rubber in the place of synthetic rubber, disease control, how to lower cost of production and solve the tapper shortage," he said.

The four-day meeting of scientists, senior planters and management company executives was organised by the International Rubber Research and Development Board (IRRDB), representing rubber research institutes in producer countries.
The board meets annually to discuss topics ranging from rubber growing to the manufacture of value-added products.
The IRRDB groups Brazil, Cameroon, China, Ivory Coast, Gabon, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Vietnam.
Natural rubber prices are expected to remain stable for the next two years and perhaps even rise as consumption increases, according to the Association of Natural Rubber Producing Countries (ANRPC).
In the long term, demand is expected to exceed supply as the world economy gathers pace, led by the booming Asia-Pacific region, it said.
Recent forecasts project a shortfall in natural rubber production compared with consumption from 2000 onwards.
